hops.title: Compare it: a floppy hose and a full one
hops.text: When the dry cups droop, show your child a garden hose. Empty, it lies flat and floppy. Full of water, it plumps up firm. Soft green stems work in a similar way, with water pushing out inside each tiny cell. Water makes up about 75 to 90 percent of the fresh weight of most lawn grasses.

sources.citation: NC State Extension, "Water Requirements of North Carolina Turfgrasses"
N.C. Cooperative Extension, Beaufort County Center, "What 'Wilting' Really Means: Heat Stress vs. Water Needs"

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A green garden hose on grass, one flat empty loop beside a plump water-filled loop, next to a pot of upright seedlings.
image.caption: Like a full hose, water inside a plant's cells holds soft stems up.

hops.title: Ask it: what is packed inside a seed
hops.text: At a check, ask, "What do you think is packed inside a seed before its leaves come out?" Children often guess tiny leaves, water or dirt. Enjoy every guess, then ask, "How could we find out?" Then share a wild seed fact: a single seed from the coco de mer palm can weigh about 40 pounds.

sources.citation: California Academy of Sciences, "Coco de Mer"

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A giant brown coco de mer palm seed beside a small paper cup of tiny green radish sprouts.
image.caption: Seeds come in every size, from tiny radish seeds to palm seeds of about 40 pounds.

hops.title: Point at it: a houseplant leaning toward the window
hops.text: Find a houseplant near a window and look together at which way its leaves point. Plants often lean toward the brightest light. In a dim spot, stems grow long and thin. Turn the pot once while your child watches, then check together as it grows to see which way the new growth points. Wash hands after touching the plant.

sources.citation: University of Minnesota Extension, "Winter houseplant tips"
University of Minnesota Extension, "Lighting for indoor plants and starting seeds"
University of Maine Cooperative Extension, "Maine Home Garden News, November"

image.alt: AI-generated illustration: A parent and child seen from behind watching a potted houseplant lean its leaves toward a sunny window.
image.caption: Houseplants often lean toward the brightest light, such as a sunny window.
